new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; if the penult vowel is schwa (ĕ) the accent goes to the final syllable instead (schwa penults are rare in Tarakan Tidung, commoner in Bolongan). Suffixation moves the accent to the new penult when the stem is vowel-final; enclitic particles do not.
new_statements.exceptions: Penults containing ĕ (schwa) do not take the accent (examples stressed on the final: tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp; Tarakan mĕnjúl) — such penults are 'extremely rare' in Tarakan. Suffixes shift accent to the new penult only when the stem ends in a vowel (nusái, naŋkúbi); in pupus-nia the original accent remains; p. 60 footnote: pa-bási 'pa being only a causative prefix, the accent falls on the second syllable'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the rule is stated for words (pronunciation of vocabulary items) and for suffixed words; §8 adds that enclitic particles (Tar. nia, Bol. na 'already') are not suffixes and do not shift the accent, so the domain is the morphological word including suffixes but excluding enclitics.
new_statements.identity_note: Beech 1908 describes two 'Tidong dialects': Tarakan (Tarakan Island, North Kalimantan = Southern Tidung, sout3241) and Bolongan (= Bulungan, a separate Glottolog language bolo1268; Glottolog cites Beech 1908 for both). Beech's p. 19 rule is stated for both dialects; Fokker's §7 gives four Tarakan examples plus three Bolongan schwa-penult examples and notes schwa penults are 'extremely rare' in Tarakan. The other opened sources cover Sebatik/Sabah Tidung (Mahali 2019, likely nort3262/itd border area) and Nunukan Tidung (Aqromi & Hendrawan 2018), none with a stress statement.

sources.note: Beech p. 19: accent falls on the penultimate 'as in Malay, Dayak, Javanese, Sundanese'; Fokker Appendix §7 p. 109: accent on the penult unless the penult contains ĕ (schwa) — examples with schwa penult are stressed on the final (tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp, mĕnjúl); §8: suffixes shift the accent to the new penult if the stem ends in a vowel; enclitic particles nia/na do not count as suffixes.
